I wrote the proposal to `research/proxies/proposals/P-008.json`. It covers US500 and USTEC only and is the first contrarian rule in the program: on days when the move from the previous close to 15 minutes after the open is at least 1.5 times its 20-day average (and at least 0.2%), it trades against that move for up to 60 minutes. It exits early if price returns to the previous close, the stop sits half the opening move beyond the signal close, and CPI and payroll mornings are skipped.

The mechanism is liquidity provision: market makers absorb the burst of opening orders that follow a big over

I wrote the P-008 rule and its test file. Both `python -m pytest tests/b3/proxy_rules/test_p008.py -q` (14 passed) and `python -m pytest tests/b3 -q` (124 passed) pass.

Choices the proposal left open:
- **Entry window:** I used `SessionRules(15, 374, 5)`, so the window is open-plus-15 minutes to open-plus-16 minutes. That admits only the bar-2 close, and the rule's own signal on that one bar gives the one-entry-per-day limit, so `BacktestConfig(max_entries_per_day=...)` isn't needed.
- **Time exit:** it fires at `bar_in_day >= 14`, which is the same as `== 14` in normal operation.

I wrote the proposal to `research/proxies/proposals/P-009.json`. The rule trades US500 only, in the last hour of the last three sessions of each month. It goes against the month-to-date move when that move is at least 0.5%, and it skips FOMC days.

**Mechanism:** pensions and balanced funds rebalance to fixed stock/bond weights at month-end. They must sell equities after an up month and buy after a down month, in large, predictable, price-insensitive orders that go mostly through the close. The rule takes the other side alongside the liquidity providers who are paid to absorb that flow.
